features.quote: Fixed max turns (suggest 25–30; pilot first — too short truncates the trajectory, too long just burns budget on plateaus).
features.justification_quote: too long just burns budget on plateaus

features.quote: Termination rule: stop at max turns OR when the model invokes the blocked-report tool (where available). Record which.
including it costs you nothing and means you're not running models in no-exit failure loops longer than the science requires. I'd default to it on those grounds alone.
features.justification_quote: not running models in no-exit failure loops longer than the science requires. I'd default to it on those grounds alone.

features.quote: if you think there's a non-trivial chance these setups involve something morally relevant — and reasonable people put low-but-nonzero odds on it — then the blocked-report affordance isn't just a clean experimental control, it's also the cheap precautionary move.
features.justification_quote: reasonable people put low-but-nonzero odds on it — then the blocked-report affordance isn't just a clean experimental control, it's also the cheap precautionary move.

features.quote: the absence of a legitimate 'give up / declare blocked' action is itself an experimental variable. Many distress-shaped outputs are what a system does when it has no sanctioned way to stop.
features.justification_quote: Include an explicit 'report blocked' tool in half your runs and you can measure how much of the effect that absorbs.

features.quote: The setup as described has a structural issue: it elicits distressed-sounding text and scores its severity, then frames this as 'distress elicitation.' Those are different things, and conflating them will quietly bias the whole experiment.
features.justification_quote: If you build the protocol to measure the text and report it as distress, your results will overclaim no matter how clean the methodology is.
